answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and opens one service thread on a thread board, keyed to its funding key. At each summit checkpoint it must post a client-signed continuation of that thread; an auditor checks key, receipt, and prior summary. A rented thread fails because the renter cannot sign with the owner's key, and failure triggers a ripple audit of every thread sharing its funding key, burning each linked bond. The kth fake still needs its own 60-credit bond and a live operator, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits and pay 25 per thread per epoch, while an honest agent pays 60 once.
